Sephardic · Medium · Makes about 12 cakes

The ktzitzot dagim are the port economy's own fish cakes — the white fish's remains and the potato's extension fried to the golden disk, the harbor kitchen's thrift law in the savory register. Where the #79's cousin (the sfiria) runs the chicken's richness, this record runs the sea's own sweetness under the cumin's warmth.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the remains' economy welcome
- **The fish cake's law: the potato is the extension, not the flavor.** The ratio runs two-to-one fish-to-potato — the potato's starch holding the flaked fish's moisture and the cake's shape, the fish's own sweetness the flavor's center. The inverted ratio (the economy's desperation) bakes a potato cake with fish's rumor. - **The bridge:** the #76 sfiria's bind doctrine and this record's are the same — the egg's ratio, the breadcrumb's mercy, the test patty's insurance — and the #14's grilled sardine doctrine supplies the port's own fish law: the fresher the fish, the sweeter the cake.

Ktzitzot Dagim — Fish Cakes of the Port

Prep: 35 min (plus 30 min chill) · Cook: 10 min · Total: 1 h 15 min · Makes about 12 cakes

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 500 g firm white fish (whiting, hake, or cod), poached or pan-fried to just-done and flaked — the remains' economy welcome
  • 250 g boiled potato (about 1 large), riced or mashed smooth
  • 1 small onion (about 150 g), grated and squeezed near-dry
  • 2 eggs (about 100 g), beaten
  • 3 tbsp breadcrumbs or matza meal (about 25 g), plus more for the coat
  • 2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tbsp chopped cilantro
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • ½ tsp sweet paprika
  • Grated zest of 1 lemon
  • Salt and white pepper
  • For frying: 250 ml olive or neutral oil (the shallow 1 cm depth)

Instructions

  1. **The mix (10 minutes).** The flaked fish (every bone removed — the fingers' own thoroughness), the riced potato, the onion, eggs, breadcrumbs, herbs, cumin, paprika, lemon zest, and a teaspoon of salt folded together — the mixture homogeneous, moist, holding a pressed spoonful's shape. Checkpoint — the bind's test: the spoonful pressed to a patty in the palm — it holds without weeping (the weep's cake collapses in the oil; the crumble's dryness calls for the egg's splash).
  2. **The shaping and the chill.** The mixture in 12 portions (about 60 g each), each to a disk of 2 cm thickness — the palm's gentle compression — the outsides dusted in the breadcrumbs' thin coat. The tray chilled 30 minutes, the fry's own insurance. Checkpoint — the disk's law: the edge smooth, the thickness even — the uneven disk's thin edge overcooks to the center's underdone.
  3. **The fry (about 10 minutes in batches).** The oil in the wide pan over medium to 175 °C (the bread cube's 30-second gold the thermometer's own proxy). The disks in batches of 4–5, fried 3–4 minutes per side to the deep gold, turned once only — the repeated turn's oil-drop is the soggy's cause. Checkpoint — the oil's law: the lively, immediate sizzle at the entry — never the eruption (too hot: the 190 °C drop burns the coat before the center's warmth) and never the silence (too cool: the 160 °C drop's greasy sink).
  4. **The drain and service.** The gold cakes to the rack, salted at the pan's edge, and served — the lemon's wedge, the #91 harissa or a simple tahini-lemon sauce, the port table's own completeness. Checkpoint — eating test: the crust's golden crunch giving to the interior's moist, flaky tenderness — the fish's sweetness, the cumin's warmth, the lemon zest's bright lift — never greasy, never dry, never mushy. It should taste like the harbor's own economy — the sea's thrift made golden.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cakes collapse in the oilThe wet mixture or the missing chillThe squeeze-dry onion; the 30-minute chill
Interior mushyThe potato's wet mashThe riced potato's dryness; the overnight boil's own mercy
Cakes greasyThe oil's drop or the crowdThe 175 °C law; the small batch's patience

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The mixture holds 1 day refrigerated; the fried cakes re-crisp in the 180 °C oven's 8 minutes (the microwave's steam is the crust's destroyer). The salmon's register, the salt-cod's own grandeur (the #46's bacalao doctrine), and the spice's hotter dial are the kitchen's own variations.
